rationale: Central bank procurement page is a recurring notice feed for payment-system, cash-handling and core-IT buys; failed verification is soft, re-check liveness.
MoF owns Treasury and state banking-service contracts; its notice page keeps producing in-scope signals.
Digital-transformation ministry tenders are the leading indicator for e-payment gateway and e-ID infrastructure.
Largest municipal buyer of banking services and POS acceptance; verified and standalone notice section.
Independent watchdog publishing recurring procurement monitoring and anomaly analysis that raw ESJN data lacks.
FOI platform and holder register: mine once as an actor map and retrieval route, not a continuous signal producer.
Static legal framework text used once to calibrate thresholds and exemptions for financial-service contracts.
Single annually-refreshed country guide chapter; useful background evidence, not a monitored feed.
Most likely domestic channel for non-ESJN/private bank-issued calls, but the useful tier sits behind a paid subscription.
E-procurement SaaS vendor rather than a notice channel; unclear whether it exposes any collectable feed.
Structured MK tender/supplier database giving the best mapped view of the IT and payments vendor pool.
Aggregator that explicitly admits private-sector publishers, but low credibility and failed fetch; re-check before approving.
Commercial alerting wrapper over ESJN data; largely redundant with the primary portal.
Official Gazette tender board carries notices from entities outside ESJN, including private buyers such as banks.
ECEPP is the key route to private MK bank procurement notices but requires a free account a human must create.
EBRD consultancy notices recurrently name MK financial-sector counterparts and winning advisers.
Group supplier rulebook binding on NLB Skopje; the governing page for vendor onboarding rules at a top-tier MK bank.
Local mirror of the group code with siblings on nlb.mk; covered by monitoring the bank's parent site.
Development bank publishing its own plans, notices and awards — the clearest visible benchmark of MK bank purchasing.
Supplier-development programme useful once for directory building; weak ongoing banking/payments signal.
Claims private-buyer RFP coverage the state portal cannot show, but low credibility and subscription-gated; verify access first.
Low-credibility reseller with similar private-tender claims; paywalled and largely redundant with c_318.
Thin aggregator advertising public and private MK contracts; worth one test but credibility is very low.
Cluster of low-quality international tender resellers, redundant cross-check value only; drop.
